title: Show attempt phase and delivery evidence in JetBrains task detail
description:
Objective: let a human see the evidence the new rules act on. Without a surface, a refused approval or a withheld dependent claim looks like an unexplained failure.

Deliverable: the JetBrains task detail panel gains a read-only Delivery block listing the current candidate's short sha and base, the latest check run's command and exit code, the delivery receipt's target and landed revision, and the owning attempt's phase. The plugin Task model in moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt gains the matching nullable fields, and a task with none of them renders exactly as it does today.

Not in scope: the full Delivery and Attention dashboard redesign, which belongs to Wave 2, board card badges, and VS Code parity. This is a minimal read-only block inside the existing detail panel, sized so the pilot is observable.

Verification: cd moe-jetbrains and ./gradlew test.
definitionOfDone: The JetBrains Task model parses the current candidate, latest check run, delivery receipt and attempt phase, with a MoeJsonTest case covering a fully populated payload
Task detail renders a Delivery block showing candidate sha and base, check command and exit code, receipt target and landed revision, and attempt phase
A task carrying none of those fields renders exactly as it does today, proven by a test
The rendering helper is a pure headless-testable function so JUnit asserts it without an IDE fixture
cd moe-jetbrains and ./gradlew test is green
taskRails: Read-only surface: no new action buttons and no approval flow changes.
Wave 2 owns the Delivery and Attention dashboard; do not build it here.
VS Code parity is a follow-up card, not part of this task.

The card's deliverable says the plugin Task model 'gains the matching nullable fields', which reads as though the daemon already sends them. It does not, and that is the single most important fact for this task. Verify it yourself rather than trusting this note. (a) grep packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts for currentCandidate, latestCheckRun, deliveryReceipt and attemptPhase: zero hits. Candidate, CheckRun, DeliveryReceipt and ExecutionAttempt are SEPARATE records under .moe/candidates, .moe/checks, .moe/receipts and .moe/attempts, keyed by candidateId or taskId. They are not fields on Task. (b) Read StateManager.getSnapshot around line 1171: it serves project, epics, tasks, workers, proposals, teams, channels and decisions. The four delivery collections are absent, so the board socket never carries them. (c) Read WebSocketServer.sendStateSnapshot around line 285 and broadcast just above it: the plugin's whole view of a task is the raw persisted Task record from that snapshot plus TASK_UPDATED events. implementationPlan.description: PROJECT THE EVIDENCE ONTO THE TASK THE BOARD IS SENT. Add a derived delivery projection in the daemon, and keep it strictly a SERVING concern: it is computed when a task is sent to a plugin client, never persisted onto the Task record and never written to disk. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/state/deliveryProjection.ts exporting one pure function that takes the state handle and a task and returns either undefined or a small object carrying the current candidate's id, short sha and base revision, the latest check run's command and exit code, the delivery receipt's target and landed revision, and the owning attempt's phase. Resolve each from the existing stores rather than re-reading disk, reusing their established selection rules: the candidate is the task's current one by createdAt then id, exactly as getContext.ts already selects it, and the check run and receipt hang off THAT candidate, not off the task, because a check or receipt belongs to a frozen candidate. Return undefined when the task has none of them, so a project that has never recorded delivery evidence produces byte-identical payloads to today, which is the third Definition-of-Done item and the compatibility guarantee for every existing client. Error handling: a missing or malformed record is treated as absent rather than throwing, because this runs inside snapshot serving on every board connect and one corrupt file must not take the socket down; log at debug and carry on. Then apply it in exactly two places in WebSocketServer.ts: sendStateSnapshot, mapping the filtered task list, and the TASK_UPDATED path in broadcast, so a live update carries the same shape as the initial snapshot. Do not touch getSnapshot itself, which other callers use and which must keep returning persisted records.

implementationPlan.description: PARSE IT IN THE JETBRAINS CLIENT. In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/model/Models.kt add a nullable delivery holder to Task plus the small data classes it needs, all with defaulted nullable members so every existing construction site and fixture keeps compiling. In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/MoeJson.kt map it in BOTH Task construction sites, the private parseTasks used by parseState and the public parseTask used for single-task messages. Forgetting the second one is the classic miss in that file and the reason a snapshot can look right while a live update silently drops the data. Parse defensively, matching what the blocker-metadata work established there: a missing, null or wrong-shaped delivery object yields null rather than throwing; each scalar is read only after a kind guard so a number never becomes an id string; the exit code is read as an integer and left null when it is not one; and no value is trimmed, normalised or reformatted, because these are identifiers a human will compare against git. Error handling is the point of this step: malformed delivery metadata must never drop the otherwise valid task it rides on, since that would blank a board column over one bad record. Reuse the strict helpers already present rather than the permissive legacy getters.

implementationPlan.description: RENDER IT, THROUGH A PURE HELPER THE TESTS CAN DRIVE. The fourth Definition-of-Done item requires the rendering decision to be a pure headless-testable function, so create moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/DeliveryPresentation.kt with no Swing and no IntelliJ imports, and declare its data types at TOP LEVEL rather than inside a companion object, because a classifier nested in a companion is not importable as Outer.Inner and has already cost this repo a failed build. It takes the parsed delivery holder and returns either nothing to show or an ordered list of label and value rows, each label a MoeBundle key rather than a literal string. Rules: show a row only when its value is actually present, so a partially populated task shows a partial block rather than empty labels; abbreviate a sha for display while keeping the full value available, since a reviewer compares the short form by eye and pastes the long one; render an exit code of zero as a pass and any non-zero as a failure, and note in a comment that a check run is what the runner REPORTED, never proof the daemon executed anything, which is the boundary the check-run card established and which this surface must not overstate. Then wire it into TaskDetailDialog.kt as a read-only block: no buttons, no actions, no approval flow changes, which is the first task rail. Reuse the existing single state listener and its disposal rather than adding a subscription, and refresh the block from the updated task so an approval or a landing is reflected without reopening the dialog. Add the message keys to moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties.

comments.author: architect-8b93cc67
comments.content:
SCOPE EXPANSION, stated up front so a reviewer judges it on the record rather than discovering it in a diff.

This card assumes the plugin can already see delivery evidence and needs only to render it. It cannot. I verified this against merged main (cf20174) before planning:

- Candidate, CheckRun, DeliveryReceipt and ExecutionAttempt are four SEPARATE record types under .moe/, keyed by candidateId or taskId. None is a field on Task. Grepping schema.ts for currentCandidate, latestCheckRun, deliveryReceipt or attemptPhase returns nothing.
- StateManager.getSnapshot (line 1171) serves project, epics, tasks, workers, proposals, teams, channels and decisions. The four delivery collections are absent, so the board socket never carries them.
- The plugin's whole view of a task is that raw persisted record, from the snapshot plus TASK_UPDATED.
- There is no per-task detail request to fetch more with: MoeCommandSender's only read messages are GET_CHANNELS, GET_MESSAGES and GET_PINS.
- get_context DOES project currentCandidate (getContext.ts:287), but that is the MCP path agents use, not the plugin's WebSocket path.

So a client-only change cannot satisfy a single Definition-of-Done item. The plan adds ONE daemon file, a serving-side projection applied in exactly two places in WebSocketServer, and that is the only scope beyond the card. Nothing is persisted onto a Task record and getSnapshot itself is untouched, because the evidence is derived from four other records and a stored copy would be a second source of truth that can go stale. That also keeps the epic's additive, migration-free rail intact.

That expansion is why the plan reports ten files and trips the size warning. Seven of them are the card's own surface plus tests; three are the projection and its test. I did not split the card, because a JetBrains surface with no data behind it is not shippable in halves.

TWO IMPLEMENTATION POINTS worth reading before starting, both of which have bitten this repo already:

1. The check run and the receipt hang off a frozen CANDIDATE, not off the task. Resolve them through the task's current candidate or the panel will show a check result from superseded bytes, which is exactly the class of lie Wave 1 exists to end. One of the required mutations targets this.

2. MoeJson has TWO Task construction sites, parseTasks for snapshots and parseTask for single-task messages. Mapping only the first makes a snapshot look correct while every live update silently drops the data. Same trap recorded during the blocker-metadata work in the same file.

Rails respected: read-only block with no actions, no Wave 2 dashboard, no VS Code. VS Code parity remains a follow-up card and should be filed once this lands, since the projection will already be serving the data it needs.

That is normal claim flow, not a bypass. The ranked pool orders by priority, so HIGH task-49ec8755 is offered ahead of this MEDIUM row while both are WORKING and unassigned.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Adding the four collections to the snapshot as sibling arrays and joining them client-side - rejected: it matches how workers and channels are served, but it pushes the current-candidate selection rule into Kotlin where it would drift from the daemon's own, and the card explicitly wants the Task model to carry the fields. Persisting the derived fields onto the Task record - rejected outright: they are derived from four other records, persisting them would create a second source of truth that can go stale, and an epic rail keeps the store additive and migration-free. Adding a per-task detail request to the plugin protocol - rejected as heavier than the card warrants and a new round trip for data the snapshot can carry. Rendering inside TaskDetailDialog without a pure helper - rejected by the fourth Definition-of-Done item and by testability: the board dialog cannot be asserted without an IDE fixture. Blocking the card until someone else adds the projection - considered, and rejected because no sibling owns it: the remaining Wave 1 rows are the wrapper receipt work and the integration pass, so blocking would strand this surface indefinitely. The honest move is to expand scope by one file and say so in the completion summary.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured on merged main (cf20174). The card contains one wrong assumption that decides the whole shape of the work: its deliverable reads as though the plugin already receives candidate, check, receipt and attempt data and merely needs to render it. It does not. Those are four separate record types under .moe/, keyed by candidateId or taskId, and none of them is a field on Task. The board socket sends exactly what getSnapshot builds - project, epics, tasks, workers, proposals, teams, channels, decisions - so the plugin's entire view of a task is the raw persisted record. There is also no per-task detail request in MoeCommandSender to fetch more with; the only read messages are GET_CHANNELS, GET_MESSAGES and GET_PINS. get_context does already project currentCandidate, but that is the MCP path agents use, not the plugin's WebSocket path. So a client-only change cannot satisfy a single Definition-of-Done item, and the scope has to grow by one daemon-side serving projection. Two details make that projection non-obvious: the check run and the receipt belong to a frozen CANDIDATE rather than to the task, so they must be resolved through the task's current candidate or a stale check will be shown against new bytes; and the projection must return nothing at all when there is no evidence, because that is what keeps existing payloads byte-identical.
planningNotes.risks: Seven files is above the five-file target, and the reason is the scope expansion in step 2 rather than drift - the worker should say so rather than let a reviewer read it as creep. The likeliest wrong implementation is resolving the check run and receipt from the task instead of from its current candidate, which would show evidence from superseded bytes, and one of the required mutations targets exactly that. The second is mapping only parseTasks and not parseTask, so snapshots look right while live updates silently drop the data; that trap is already recorded from the blocker-metadata work in the same file. Keep the projection serving-only: nothing persisted, nothing written, and getSnapshot itself untouched since other callers depend on it. A project with no delivery evidence must produce byte-identical payloads, which is both the compatibility guarantee and a Definition-of-Done item. Do not overstate what a check run proves - it is runner-reported, not daemon-executed. Respect the rails: no actions in the block, no Wave 2 dashboard, no VS Code. On this box a Gradle run can report an out-of-memory in its cleanup thread when the temp directory is large, which is cosmetic after BUILD SUCCESSFUL but worth raising the client heap for, and the shared Gradle slot must be serialised through the resource protocol.

rejectionHistory.reason:
DoD 2 fails silently for store-valid evidence. isSha at deliveryProjection.ts:17 accepts only 40 hex, and line 41 applies it to Candidate.treeSha and baseRevision. The store and the documented moe.record_candidate contract accept 7-40 hex (candidateStore.ts:41 SHA_RE via requireSha, checkRunStore.ts:43, docs/MCP_SERVER.md:656-657). A candidate with a 7-39 character sha is thrown as malformed, logged at debug only, and dropped together with its check and receipt. With no open attempt, the Delivery block disappears entirely. get_context.currentCandidate, the qa_approve candidate gate and policy.ts all act on that same candidate, so the panel contradicts the rules it exists to explain.

Repro on HEAD 2fb9593, in a scratch git-archive tree: validateCandidateParams accepted treeSha = baseRevision at lengths 7, 12, 39 and 40, and listCandidatesForTask picked it each time. With a check on the same tree (exit 0), a 40-hex receipt and a closed owning attempt, deliveryProjection returned undefined for 7, 12 and 39. Only length 40 got the full object.

To pass:
(1) Align the candidate predicate with the store contract: reuse or export its SHA_RE, and keep landedRevision at 40 hex to match receiptStore.
(2) Add a projection test that fails on the current code. It should seed a short store-valid candidate with a check and receipt, and assert the full projection. Every fixture today is 40 hex.
(3) Re-run the daemon suite, tsc and ./gradlew test.
